A1.justification: Both readable 21-page PDFs describe SpikeGen, despite the changed title. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original pretraining ablations and quantitative and qualitative experiments on deblurring, frame reconstruction, and novel-view synthesis, including supplementary analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains original results for all three downstream tasks and appendix analyses, and reports an additional ImageNet comparison in Figure 1.

M1.justification: The S3 encoder, VAE, modality mixing, color-faded targets, simultaneous token generation, and spike-alignment fine-tuning remain unchanged. Section 3.3 replaces 'MSE' with 'diffusion loss', but diffusion was already specified in v1's methods and pipeline; this does not establish a changed objective.

E1.justification: Both versions use ImageNet, GOPRO, SREDS, momVidarReal2021, and the object-centric and outdoor Blender datasets for the same tasks. V2's biological and infrared examples are motivation, not additional evaluated domains.

E2.justification: V2 Figure 1 adds S-SDM as an ImageNet comparator; v1's ImageNet quantitative comparison contained only SpikeGen step-count variants. Comparator membership in the three downstream benchmark tables and retained appendix comparisons is unchanged.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported pretraining preparation from generating eight spike frames per image to randomly selecting eight from 64 generated frames. This revises the stated preprocessing while retaining eight input frames. Downstream splits, metrics, and Appendix B training budgets remain unchanged; rerunning experiments is not established.

E4.justification: V1 Table 1 tests whether replacing 64 autoregressive steps with one step preserves quality. V2 removes this ablation rather than relocating it, although Section 3.2 still invokes it through an unresolved appendix reference. The modality, pseudo-dense-frame, limited-spike, and two-stage analyses in Appendix C remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, evaluation seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The reporting practice remains point estimates and qualitative examples.

E6.justification: V2 Figure 1 newly reports ImageNet PSNR/SSIM of 20.11/0.61 for SpikeGen and 16.70/0.49 for S-SDM. V1 Table 1's step-count results, including PSNR 18.79 and 19.08, disappear. These are not established as matched-setting performance improvements. Corresponding downstream tables and retained appendix results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The spike-formation equations, TFI/TFP definitions, latent diffusion objective, modality-mixing equations, and appendix metric definitions are retained. No theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: V2 adds an explicit aim to emulate rod/cone decoupling and cortical latent processing, recasting contribution 1 around biological inspiration. The central claims of pioneering latent generative RGB–spike fusion and effectiveness across the same three tasks remain, limiting the change in scientific contribution scope.

C2.justification: V2 adds biological mechanism explanations for multimodal latent processing. Section 4.2 changes the described SpikeGS trade-off from inaccurate brightness matching to inaccurate color-saturation matching. The clear-input 3DGS upper-bound qualification disappears, while Appendix D's model-size and inference-hardware limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 adds a repository link for SpikeGen code and pretrained weights in the abstract. It removes v1's explicit 256 × 256 pretraining image size and the stated source of the clear-input 3DGS scores. Hardware, optimizer, model hyperparameters, and training-budget tables remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The research positioning shifts substantially from shutter limitations and camera-engineering alternatives toward biological vision and latent self-supervised learning. V2 adds neuroscience and RGB–infrared fusion references and a new SSL discussion covering SimMIM, iBOT, and DINOv3, while removing much of the earlier hardware-oriented literature.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, much of the introduction, contribution framing, and conclusion are extensively rewritten, and Related Works gains an SSL subsection. Most technical and appendix prose is retained. V2 also introduces unresolved appendix figure/table references in Section 3.2.

P2.justification: V2 adds an overview Figure 1 and substantially expands the pipeline diagram as Figure 2, illustrating the S3 encoder and modality control. V1's separate MAR comparison diagram and ablation table disappear. Benchmark displays are redistributed, and Figure 4 becomes side-by-side while its caption still describes top and bottom panels.

improvement.justification: V2 adds useful pipeline illustrations, an ImageNet baseline comparison, and a code/weights pointer. However, it removes quantitative support for the retained simultaneous-generation claim, leaves unresolved appendix references, and drops the clear-input 3DGS provenance and upper-bound explanation. The new ImageNet comparison lacks a separately described baseline protocol, while the established downstream evidence is unchanged. These gains and losses do not support a reliable net quality judgment.
